name: Petri Net Reduction
author: István Koren
description: Removes the scaffolding from an accepting Petri net without changing what it does. A converted or discovered net carries a place per sequence flow and a silent transition per gateway — structure the construction needed and the process does not. Reduction fuses it away, and the promise is exact: the reduced net produces the same sequences of activities, and accepts the same ones. That is checked on every build by enumerating both nets' languages with the play-out plugin.

actions.label: Reduce net
actions.description: Applies the classical structural reductions — fusion of series and parallel places and transitions, elimination of self-loop places, removal of redundant places — to a fixpoint, keeping only the ones that preserve the net's language. Every visible activity survives; only silent scaffolding and redundant places go. The result is an ordinary Accepting Petri Net: it renders, replays, aligns and plays out like any other.

agent.whenToUse: After converting a BPMN diagram or a process tree to a Petri net, or before a state-space search: fewer places and silent transitions make soundness checking, alignment and play-out all cheaper, and the diagram readable.
agent.notFor: Simplifying a model in the sense of dropping behaviour. Nothing here removes an activity or a path — if the net was unreadable because the process is complex, it will still be.
examples: the default settings on a net converted from BPMN, which is where the scaffolding is
dropImplicit false to keep every place and only fuse silent steps

dropSilent.title: Remove silent steps that do nothing
dropSilent.description: A silent transition whose inputs and outputs are the same leaves the marking exactly as it was and records nothing. It can only lengthen a firing sequence.

fuseSeries.title: Fuse steps in series
fuseSeries.description: A silent transition between two others, or between two places, collapses: the pair can only ever happen one after the other, and nothing observable separates them. This is where most of a converted net's size goes.

fuseParallel.title: Fuse duplicates
fuseParallel.description: Two transitions with the same label, inputs and outputs are one transition; two places wired identically to the same transitions are one place. A trace cannot tell them apart.

dropSelfLoops.title: Remove self-loop places
dropSelfLoops.description: A place a transition borrows a token from and immediately returns holds a count that never changes. If it starts with enough tokens it constrains nothing.

dropImplicit.title: Remove redundant places
dropImplicit.description: A place another place already constrains — it never is the reason a transition cannot fire, and it says the same thing about finishing. Turn this off to keep the net's places exactly as they were and only fuse silent structure.

citation.text: Murata, T. (1989). Petri nets: properties, analysis and applications. Proceedings of the IEEE 77(4), 541-580 — the six classical reduction rules are §5. Berthelot, G. (1986), Transformations and decompositions of nets, Advances in Petri Nets, LNCS 254, 359-376, is the reference for behaviour-preserving transformation; implicit places follow Colom, J.M. and Silva, M. (1990), Improving the linearly based characterization of P/T nets.
